name: Humanitarian funding gap
value: WFP Gaza ration cuts; no full suspension
summary: WFP has cut Gaza food aid by about a third and halved rations; no large-scale suspension in a famine-risk country found
state: WFP said on 19 Oct that funding cuts forced it to reduce Gaza food assistance from 1.6 million to 1.1 million people a month and halve rations, and that it needs $450 million to March 2027 (WFP). The IRC said on 13 Oct that donors must scale up food, health and nutrition funding as famine risk rises in Darfur and Kordofan. Major ration cuts meet Watch; searches on 22 Nov found no large-scale suspension of food or health aid in a famine-risk country.
for_you: No direct effect for most UK readers. Funding gaps mean fewer people reached in Gaza, Sudan and other crises; OCHA's Financial Tracking Service publishes appeal coverage.
rubric_hit: Major ration cuts announced (WFP Gaza) = Watch; no large-scale suspension

sources.title: WFP — Funding cuts force WFP to drastically reduce lifesaving assistance in Gaza
IRC — War and El Niño-driven drought deplete food stocks, pushing Sudan further towards famine

why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.
